body L18: Addenda, p. LXXVII («297,18»): the use of the lunar stations in astrological prognostics is set out by Albohazen Haly, De iudiciis astrorum, Basel 1571, part VII, ch. 101, pp. 342-46 («de electionibus secundum motum Lunae per mansiones»), and by al-Būnī, Shams al-ma‘ārif (on the magical sciences), [Cairo] 1291 H., t. I, pp. 16-24, who also gives (pp. 23-24) extracts from the sayings of the old Arabs (asǵā‘ al-‘arab) after one al-Kindī: «قال بعضهم قرأت على شيخنا الكندي رحمه الله تعالى قال قرأت على ابي منصور الحوالة قال بلغني عن ابي محمد المناوي انه قال تقول العرب الخ»; Abū Ma‘shar had written a special booklet on elections according to the lunar stations (al-ikhtiyārāt ‘alà manāzil al-qamar).
body L19-L22: «Thibaut» is letter-spaced; the dash of «13–16» is joined to the 3 and is long (about 6 pt).
body L23: the dash after «e)» measures 9.6 pt, the hyphen of «6-7» 3.4 pt.

body L26-L33: «al–Battānī» (L29) and «aṣ–Ṣūfī» (L30) are letter-spaced, «d’al–maǵisṭī» and «d’al–Battānī» are not; their long dashes measure 4.9 to 5.3 pt. Addenda, p. LXXVII («297,e»): two examples of mizāǵ in this sense in Steinschneider, Zur Gesch. der Uebersetzungen aus dem Indischen (ZDMG XXV, 1871, p. 400), who also notes mimsāk kōl kōkāb, «the mixture of each star», that is its situation, in the Hebrew writings of Abraham ibn ‘Ezra (d. February 1167); but he wrongly compares al-mumāzaǵāt (the title of a book of Abū Ma‘shar after Ibn al-Qifṭī) and al-mumāzaǵāt bi ’l-ittiṣālāt, the «commixtures [of the planets] arising from the applications», that is the aspects of the planets to one another (opposition, quadrature, trine, sextile), on which al-Battānī ch. LIV, p. 129 sqq. In Lippert's edition, p. 154, the title of Abū Ma‘shar's book is al-mizāǵāt, as in an-Nadīm, p. 277, l. 17 (Suter's version, p. 32: «Das Buch der Temperamente»); if the reading is true, mizāǵ has the sense of mumāzaǵah, the verbal noun of the third form. The first chapter (faṣl) of the fifth treatise of aṣ-Ṣūfī's unpublished Introduction to judgements (al-madkhal fī ’l-aḥkām) is «on the commixtures of the planets and the exposition of the ways of judgements» (fī mumāzaǵāt al-kawākib wa dhikr ṭuruq al-aḥkām).

body L26-L33: Nallino's addenda et emendanda in Part II (pp. XVIII-XIX; AB01-PDF0435-body-L014 to AB01-PDF0436-body-L019), on Part I, p. LXXVIII and this page, show the astrological use of mumāzaǵah and mizāǵ: Abū Ma‘shar, Kitāb al-qirānāt (the preface speaks of the conjunctions of the planets in the twelve signs and of their mumāzaǵāt with one another through the applications, and a table gives the applications of the upper planets and their mumāzaǵāt with the lower); Abū Naṣr al-Qummī, al-Bāri‘, tract V, chapter I (the effects of the planets in the mumāzaǵāt); at-Tahānawī, Dictionary of technical terms, ed. Sprenger, p. 1386 (the aspects of the Moon are called its imtizāǵāt or mumāzaǵāt); Naṣīr ad-dīn aṭ-Ṭūsī, al-mukhtaṣar fī ‘ilm at-tanǵīm, chapter XIII (the mizāǵāt of the Moon with the planets); Ulugh Beg, p. 119 of the text, 164 of the translation (a table of the mizāǵāt of the Moon with the planets, promised for its applications). Mumāzaǵah, and more rarely mizāǵ, are thus the applications of the planets to one another or to the Moon. The Greeks used σύγκρασις in this sense (Pseudo-Proclus on the Tetrabiblos, p. 76; Vettius Valens; a Laurentian codex in Boll, Sphaera, p. 10), more rarely μῖξις (Palchus); Firmicus Maternus says mixtura (ed. Kroll, I, 2 and I, 4), the Syriac mūzāgā (Bardesanes, The Book of the Laws of Countries, ed. Nau, Paris 1899, pp. 18-19 of the text, 44 of the translation). Among astrologers mizāǵ also means the temperament or nature of each heavenly body, as in the Arabic Tetrabiblos quoted in Part II, p. 290. A note adds that the Latin De magnis coniunctionibus of Albumasar (Augsburg 1489) is not this Kitāb al-qirānāt but the Kitāb fīhi ǵumal min dalālāt al-ashkhāṣ al-‘alawiyyah, as Steinschneider and Loth saw.
